articles.title: Watch John Cena Perform Iconic WWE Entrance Theme 'The Time Is Now' in Trending Video
articles.summary: WWE legend John Cena's rapping days are well behind him, but he showed that he's still got it.
articles.body:
WWE legend John Cena's rapping days are well behind him, but he showed that he's still got it.

Cena was seen performing his iconic "The Time Is Now" entrance music during a recent radio appearance, and he didn't miss a lyric:

WWE Moments That Could Be Horror Movies 😱

Cena famously adopted a hip-hop persona during his "Dr. of Thuganomics" era, but it wasn't just for show. WWE veteran and longtime music artist R-Truth previously told B/R that he and Cena recorded an unreleased song together years ago, and he cherishes the memory to this day.

Cena is currently on the promotional trail for his new film, Matchbox: The Movie , which was released on Oct. 9 on Apple TV.

articles.title: Top 10 NFL Coordinators Ready To Become Head Coaches
articles.summary: We identify the NFL coordinators who are the top head-coaching candidates and break down why they're on our list.
articles.body: Head coaches are already firmly on the hot seat this season. These coordinators are the names to pay attention to. There were 10 new head coaches entering this season, including a few surprising changes like Sean McDermott being out in Buffalo or John Harbaugh in Baltimore. Veterans like Todd Bowles (Buccaneers), Jim Harbaugh (Chargers) and Dan Quinn (Commanders) are potentially on thin ice after slow starts to the season. Fans will be wondering who might be the next man up to lead their team. Who could be the coordinators who replace those head coaches on the hot seat? Here are the 10 names you need to know before the coaching carousel begins this offseason. 10. Jeff UlbrichFalcons Defensive Coordinator Why He’s A Candidate Ruiz: Ulbrich has been a fringe head-coaching candidate since serving as Jets defensive coordinator under Robert Saleh. Nothing has changed since he parted ways with his former boss, and Ulbrich has strengthened his résumé by running the Falcons' defense. He got above-average results from a young Atlanta defense in 2025 and had the unit playing at a top-10 clip by season’s end. Atlanta pummeling Josh Allen and derailing his MVP campaign on "Thursday Night Football" was one of the season's biggest shocks and put Ulbrich back on the head-coaching radar. Ulbrich isn’t a flashy defensive playcaller. You won't find exotic blitzes and fancy coverages on the Falcons' defensive tape. But you will find a defense that’s structurally sound and always plays hard. Atlanta has punched well above its weight defensively since Ulbrich’s arrival. What We’re Hearing Vacchiano: "I’ve always wondered why he doesn’t get more play [in head coaching hiring cycles]. His defenses are always tough, and his players really respond to him," an NFL executive told me. "I mean, what he did with the Jets [as defensive coordinator from 2021-24], when the offense gave them no help at all, was a miracle. I know Robert Saleh gets credit for that, but it was really Ulbrich leading them. "And don’t discount what he did as interim [head coach for the Jets in 2024] either. That team was a mess. The whole organization was dysfunctional. And he kept a team with a lot of strong personalities from completely tearing itself apart. He’s under the radar, but he’s going to be a terrific head coach someday if someone gives him a chance." 9. Ejiro EveroPanthers Defensive Coordinator Why He’s A Candidate McKenna: He first burst onto the scene in 2022 in Denver when his chops with X’s and O’s started to turn heads. But the defense faltered late in the year, in part because of shaky leadership at the top from former Broncos head coach Nathaniel Hackett. That meant Evero had to find a new home, and the Panthers scooped him up. And it speaks to his impressive acumen that he has remained the DC in Carolina despite coaching turnover, working for former Panthers coach Frank Reich and current coach Dave Canales. The numbers haven’t been pretty for a substantial portion of Evero’s time in Carolina, because the defensive personnel has been … quite bad. But GM Dan Morgan has invested in that side of the ball, and the Panthers have bona fide stars in cornerback Jaycee Horn and defensive lineman Derrick Brown. They also seem to have a few newcomers on the rise, from linebacker Devin Lloyd to edge Jaelan Phillips. Phillips and Horn are dealing with injuries. But this group could ascend quickly — and help the Panthers make the playoffs. If/when that happens, Evero will get the respect that’s overdue. What We’re Hearing Williams: Considered a head-coaching candidate since his time with the Rams under McVay, where he rose from safeties coach to passing game coordinator, Evero has coached a top-10 defense two times over the past five years as a DC. The 45-year-old remains an up-and-coming head coaching candidate. Evero interviewed for vacancies with the Falcons, Steelers and Raiders during the last hiring cycle. "He is a smart, strong leader respected by the team and carries himself like an alpha," one league personnel executive, who worked in the same building as Evero, told me. 8. Anthony WeaverRavens Defensive Coordinator Why He’s A Candidate McKenna: The more you look at Weaver's work with the Dolphins, the more you’ll see that he achieved something special. We’re seeing former Miami head coach Mike McDaniel’s reputation dissolve with every interception and sack from Justin Herbert. So if you look back, you’ll have even more respect for how Weaver quietly produced a strong Miami defense in 2024. It's even more impressive considering he took over after the strange exit by Vic Fangio, who was Miami's DC in 2023. And so that informs the Ravens’ defensive success. It’s an aging unit — not unlike the rest of the roster. But he (and defensive-minded head coach Jesse Minter) are getting the most out of the players. If Baltimore’s defense keeps getting better as the year goes on, Weaver should graduate to his first head coaching job. What We’re Hearing Vacchiano: "What I hear over and over about him is ‘leader of men,’" an NFL assistant GM told me. "I know it’s an overused cliché, but he comes across as powerful and in charge. I’ve heard that from a bunch of teams that interviewed him in recent years. That can matter almost as much as strategy. And he’s good at that part, too. But when he’s in front of a room, his players listen. And they believe." 7. Klay Kubiak49ers Offensive Coordinator Why He’s A Candidate Ruiz: It’s easy to write off Klay Kubiak as just another Kyle Shanahan assistant. Having taken his first pro coaching job in 2021, he doesn’t have a long NFL track record. He’s never called plays above the high school level. And with Shanahan calling plays for the 49ers, it’s unclear exactly what Kubiak's job entails as offensive coordinator. But the 49ers offense has taken massive steps forward since Kubiak took over the job in 2025. Shanahan’s run game is more diverse than ever, and the pre-snap motion and player usage have been more creative over the past two seasons. Even if Kubiak isn’t relaying the plays to QB Brock Purdy, he deserves some credit for this recent glow-up. The offense looks like a machine in Kubiak’s second season as the coordinator. And don’t sleep on his Year 1 work, when he helped the offense stay afloat despite numerous injuries, including a high-ankle sprain that knocked Purdy out for seven weeks. What We’re Hearing Williams: The younger brother of Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak and son of former longtime NFL head coach Gary Kubiak, Klay is a former high school teacher and head coach who steadily ascended from defensive quality control assistant to offensive coordinator during his six years with the 49ers. "Klay is one of the best coaches I’ve ever been around," former San Francisco quarterbacks coach Brian Griese told me. "He has a lot of his dad in him — really smart and able to communicate well. He was a teacher, so you have someone who has character and values that he lives every single day, and the players can see he genuinely cares about them. And he has the acumen and the mind to really execute and innovate and be ahead of other coaches on the defensive side." 6. Chris ShulaRams Defensive Coordinator Why He’s A Candidate McKenna: Look at the way Shula had the Rams — without Aaron Donald or Myles Garrett — punishing Eagles QB Jalen Hurts on third down in Week 4. Look at the way Shula had the Rams deceiving Bo Nix in Week 3 to the point where the Broncos QB looked lost — throwing five turnover-worthy passes, even if the Rams only secured one (and errantly got a DPI on the other). Shula has put together some of the more dominant defensive game plans in the NFL over the past two years. That’s no doubt partially because of all the talent he’s had. And given all that talent, Shula’s defenses should probably be a little bit more consistent. But he has demonstrated the acumen and upside that teams will want in a defensive coach. What We’re Hearing Williams: The grandson of the winningest head coach in NFL history in Don Shula, Chris Shula brings a legacy of coaching to the job. He’s coached with good friend and former Miami of Ohio teammate Sean McVay for the past decade, so he’s learned how to build a culture from one of the best. Shula also cut his teeth learning from the likes of Wade Phillips, Raheem Morris and Brandon Staley, so he brings with him a diversity of defensive schemes that he can implement. "He has been on some good staffs at different levels and certainly has been successful with the Rams," a scout who worked in the same building as Shula told me. "But I’ve seen young coaches become head coaches too soon, just from the depth of life and football experience, which is usually a precursor for success as a head coach. But Chris always seemed like a squared-away dude when I knew him." 5. Nate ScheelhaaseRams Offensive Coordinator Why He’s A Candidate Ruiz: Anyone in Sean McVay’s orbit is going to get interest during the hiring cycle. After just two years on the Rams' staff, Scheelhaase earned three interviews for head coaching gigs last offseason, and it feels like a matter of time before he lands a head job after being promoted to McVay’s offensive coordinator. Scheelhaase is a smart, diligent coach by all accounts, but with just a year of college playcalling experience, it’s unclear what he’ll bring to a team as an offensive mind. Will he even call plays? If so, will he be any good at it? That never stopped teams from hiring offensive coordinators away from McVay’s staff. Kevin O’Connell got the Vikings' job with no playcalling experience. The same goes for Zac Taylor in Cincinnati. Liam Coen and Matt LaFleur had to leave McVay’s nest to call plays elsewhere, but both proved qualified when they got their chance to lead a team. Hiring McVay’s assistants has been a trend for nearly a decade, and teams that jumped on it seem happy with the decision. O’Connell, LaFleur, Coen and Zac Taylor are all still employed. Even if "proximity to McVay" is Scheelhaase’s only notable qualification, that could be enough for coach-needy teams. What We’re Hearing Williams: League sources I spoke with said Scheelhaase interviewed well during the last head coaching cycle. I wrote a profile on Scheelhaase at the start of the regular season, and the head coaches he worked for in college and the pros spoke glowingly of his work ethic and ability to connect with players. "He’s got great organizational skills, great communication skills," Rams head coach Sean McVay told me. "He shows great leadership to be able to bring people together. He’s got a great capacity for the game, and he’s continuing to learn the foundation of some of the things we’ve been doing. But he’s been awesome. I’ve been really pleased with the job he’s done." 4. Grant UdinskiJaguars Offensive Coordinator Why He’s A Candidate McKenna: Ever since Liam Coen arrived, Trevor Lawrence has elevated into the player we thought he’d be: a top-tier and (most importantly) consistent QB. Quietly, behind the scenes, the 30-year-old Udinski has watched and learned. But it’s not a passive gig for him. He has also participated heavily in the quarterback’s progress. Maybe he hasn’t made the move that Doyle made — jumping laterally to a different OC job to take over playcalling — but that doesn’t mean Udinski isn’t turning heads. Last interview season, he impressed people around the league. And with the Jaguars off to an even crisper start on offense, there’s so much to like about Udinski’s candidacy in a league that was — last year at least — starved for young offensive minds. Ultimately, Udinski's candidacy will be based on Lawrence’s performance and upward trajectory. If that holds, he’ll likely be a head coach in 2027. What We’re Hearing "He’s really young — like Sean McVay young when he was hired. There’s no doubt he’s a rising star, and everyone is always looking for the next McVay," an NFL assistant GM told me. "But I think he’s going to need to get a little more experience. He might need to get away from Jacksonville, too. It might be hard for some to get past the perception that Liam Coen is the brains down there. Maybe that’s unfair, but it’s also why he might need to succeed somewhere else first." 3. Anthony CampanileJaguars Defensive Coordinator Why He’s A Candidate Ruiz: Watch Anthony Campanile run one team meeting, and you’ll get it. The guy can fire up a room. And he’s much more than some rah-rah meathead. The dude knows ball. You can see it in the design of the Jaguars' defense. It checks all the boxes for a modern scheme. Jacksonville stops the run without sacrificing coverage. On obvious passing downs, Campanile has several pitches to throw at an opposing quarterback. He’ll play man, he’ll play safe zones, he’ll send overload blitzes and simulated pressures. It is not easy to prepare for. More importantly, Campanile has gotten results wherever he’s been. He was hired as Packers run game coordinator in 2024 and immediately fixed Green Bay’s run defense, which finished third in yards per attempt. Liam Coen brought him to Jacksonville in 2025, and the Jaguars' defense went from one of the league's worst units to an above-average outfit. The results have been even better in 2026. Consistent, linear improvement is a sign of good coaching. What We’re Hearing Vacchiano: "I hate going up against his defenses," an NFL offensive assistant coach told me. "They’re hard to predict. He’s coached under Vic Fangio and Brian Flores and you can see the influence from both of them. And he’s great at adjusting based on what he thinks you’re going to do. The way they’re playing, a lot of NFL teams will take notice." "Still a little light on experience, but you can’t argue with the job he’s done with that Jacksonville defense," an NFL executive told me. "And it’s only a matter of time before the NFL starts picking apart that staff. His defenses are unpredictable, and his players play for him. I’d want to see more, but he’s going to get a lot of interviews." 2. Declan DoyleRavens Offensive Coordinator Why He’s A Candidate Henry McKenna: As a case study for how Doyle has been one step ahead of defenses all year, look at his usage of receiver Zay Flowers. The 30-year-old first-year Ravens OC has conceived of seemingly endless concepts to get Flowers open on the same crossing route. Doyle just has a way of putting elaborate window dressing on simple plays — and the flourish and sleight-of-hand have made the Ravens extremely successful. Doyle’s influences include Ben Johnson in Chicago and Sean Payton in both New Orleans and Denver. He spent a few years as a tight ends coach before jumping into an offensive coordinator role in 2025 with the Bears. He then followed Ravens coach Jesse Minter to Baltimore in order to get a playcalling job on top of his OC duties. And it has been a smart move for Doyle to step away from Johnson’s shadow. Neither of them seem to be suffering. What We’re Hearing Ralph Vacchiano: "We love the hot offensive coach in this league, so he’ll get a [head-coaching] job eventually," an NFL executive told me. "Maybe soon. But [next year] might be a little too quick. Let’s be honest, it was Ben Johnson running the [Bears'] offense last year, not [Doyle]. I’m not diminishing what he did. But let’s see him on his own for a couple of years first. "That said, I can see why so many wanted him as offensive coordinator. He learned from one of the best, and he’s obviously got a great offensive mind. But let’s give him a little time to develop into a leader." 1. Brian FloresVikings Defensive Coordinator Why He’s A Candidate Steven Ruiz: No defensive coordinator has done more with less since Flores started calling plays for the Vikings in 2023. Minnesota finished in the top seven in points allowed in 2024 and 2025, and it’s leading the league this season. Flores has accomplished that feat with just one All-Pro player (Danielle Hunter in 2023) and two Pro Bowlers (Andrew Van Ginkel and Jonathan Grennard in 2024). And as the roster continues to churn — Hunter and Greenard have both been replaced with younger, cheaper players — the results just keep on improving. If Flores’ defense isn’t the best in the NFL, it’s certainly the most feared. It’s a nightmare for quarterbacks, who face incessant blitzing from every angle. It’s controlled chaos. Flores isn’t just sending the house recklessly. He has a strong handle on opponents’ protection plans and always finds the weak points. There are no questions about Flores’ X’s and O’s. He’s one of the league's top defensive minds, but that’s just one part of the job. After Flores clashed with several Dolphins players as Miami head coach from 2019-21, including first-round quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, questions remain about his ability to lead a locker room. Flores has said all the right things since his failed stint in Miami. He’s talked about evolving his teaching methods, and players in Minnesota, where he essentially acts as a second head coach under Kevin O’Connell, go to bat for him. When I visited Vikings camp last summer, several veteran players told me they came to Minnesota specifically to play for Flores. The players rave about his coaching style as much as his scheme. What We’re Hearing Eric D. Williams: Arguably the top defensive coordinator in the league, Flores won more games than he lost in two of his three seasons as head coach of the Dolphins. "Not only will he have an opportunity, but he will also be much more selective this time," a league source told me. "He knows what exactly he is looking for. And he has already been a head coach, so being a head coach is not his dream job like it is for other coaches who have never been one before." Flores might already be a head coach if not for his ongoing systemic racial discrimination litigation with the league. And according to sources I spoke with, he has softened his abrasive approach to leading a team from his time in South Beach. "He is one of the most thoughtful and creative coaches I have ever been around," a longtime personnel man who worked in the building with Flores told me. "He deserves a second chance. He learned from his past, but owners are holding his lawsuit against him in my opinion."

articles.title: FC Barcelona eyes €300 million and more in annual retail revenue under record Nike partnership until 2038
articles.summary: FC Barcelona is currently aiming to generate more than €300 million pounds per season from its retail and licensing business as part of its expanded
articles.body: FC Barcelona is currently aiming to generate more than €300 million pounds per season from its retail and licensing business as part of its expanded partnership with Nike. The ambitious target forms the club's long-term strategy to boost its commercial operation, expand its global reach, and increase its revenue from Nike's merchandise sales.As per reports, Barcelona announced its renewed strategic partnership with Nike in November 2024, describing it as a new beginning of a relationship that began in 1998. The agreement was subsequently ratified by the club members in December 2024, and again it became effective from the 2024-25 season.It is to be noted that this agreement is the largest sponsorship deal in its history. According to Fabrizio Romano, the president of Barcelona, he stated, “The new contract with Nike is 3x more valuable than the previous one. It’s the biggest contract in football world for technical sponsor partnership.”FC Barcelona aims to expand retail and licensing revenue to €300 million with their partner NikeFC Barcelona and Nike have renewed a strategic alliance to ensure the global development of the Club's Retail and Licensing business. According to earlier reports, Barcelona has set an initial target of reaching €200 million per season in retail and licensing revenue before exceeding €300 million in the medium term.Also, under the renewed arrangement, Nike will work alongside Barça Licensing & Merchandising (BLM), the club’s subsidiary responsible for licensing and merchandising, to develop products, improve supply-chain operations and strengthen global distribution.The agreement between FC Barcelona and Nike is structured in three main strategic areas are sponsorship rights, product licensing, and support for retail and eCommerce operations. Basically, the contract allows Barcelona to develop its own branded merchandise and pursue strategic partnerships with brands outside Nike’s competing technical-product category.In February 2026, Barcelona reported that UEFA’s annual club report had placed its kit and merchandising revenue at a record €277 million, €46 million ahead of the second-ranked club. Barcelona credited its renewed Nike partnership and the expansion of its retail and e-commerce operations as important factors behind that growth. Even the increase in revenue was reported well above the industry average, with indicators that double or even triple typical market standards.The €300 million target therefore represents a further step in Barcelona’s ambition to maximise the value of its global brand. However, the growth will depend on the increased sales of the official merchandise, international retail expansion and the club’s ability to convert its worldwide fan base into commercial growth.With Nike’s long-term partnership, Barcelona will look to build on its existing merchandising business and establish retail and licensing as an increasingly significant source of recurring revenue.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Phillies President Dave Dombrowski Stresses Trea Turner 'Has To Be Better'
articles.summary: Philadelphia Phillies president Dave Dombrowski voiced his displeasure with shortstop Trea Turner's 2026 performance.
articles.body: By his standards, Trea Turner had arguably the worst season of his MLB career in 2026. What's more, Philadelphia Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski is being brutally honest about the team's star shortstop. "We were very clear. He knows he has to be better at shortstop. And I told him that it's really mandatory that he’s like that," Dombrowski said about Turner's 2026 performance at a press conference at Citizens Bank Park on Thursday morning, according to MLB.com. "He feels he can play, and if he plays shortstop like he did in ’25, he can play shortstop. But if he plays it like he did in ’26, he can't. And he totally understands that." Turner posted -17 defensive runs saved (DRS) at shortstop this season, marking the third time in Turner's four years with the Phillies that he has finished with a negative, double-digit DRS. Meanwhile, Turner, a two-time batting champion and three-time All-Star, totaled 19 home runs, 58 RBIs, 21 stolen bases, an 81 OPS+ and -0.1 wins above replacement (WAR), while posting a .242/.297/.378 slash line. Turner's batting average, on-base percentage, slugging percentage, OPS+ and WAR were all career worsts over a full season. Just last season (2025), Turner led the National League with a .304 batting average and posted 5.4 wins above replacement. "The reason we signed him at the beginning compared to some others, not only was he a good player, but we thought that he had the ability to continue to be a good player for a longer time period because of his quick-twitch muscles, the type of athlete he is, what he possesses," Dombrowski said of Turner. "I mean, he led the league in hitting last year, so I was surprised myself on the offensive year that he had and that we weren't able to get out of it, as he was, so it's up to us to try to fix all those types of things. "We’ve already given [Turner] some information ourselves that we think could be helpful. … We need to leave it that he is very willing to do, if he doesn't play shortstop, what is best for the Philadelphia Phillies organization. So, that's how we left it with him, and he's determined to show us that he can play it. And I said, ‘You have to show it. You cannot play shortstop like [you] did defensively in ’26, going into ’27.'" The 33-year-old Turner is four years into an 11-year, $300 million contract with the Phillies. As for other positions, Turner primarily played second base for the Los Angeles Dodgers down the stretch of the 2021 MLB season and has made 79 career starts at the keystone. He also started 44 games in center field for the Washington Nationals in 2016. Granted, Turner, aside from being the team's designated hitter, hasn't played a position outside shortstop since 2021. articles.title: Big 10 Pick 6: Bring to a Gentle Boil
articles.summary: I went 0-6 against the spread two weeks ago and bounced back to 5-1 last week, missing on the crazy Minnesota letdown against Purdue. That brings me near eve...
articles.body:
I went 0-6 against the spread two weeks ago and bounced back to 5-1 last week, missing on the crazy Minnesota letdown against Purdue. That brings me near even at 17-19 ATS on the year. Another good week can get me back in the black, so let's get straight to the picks.

Before the season, the idea that the Dawgs would be underdogs in this game would have seemed unfathomable. The Huskies were ranked #17 in the country and Purdue hadn't won a conference game roughly since Joe Tiller and Drew Brees played in West Lafayette. Now, the Boilermakers have won two in a row (that's a streak!) against Illinois and Minnesota- the very same Gophers team that pantsed UW at home in the conference opener. They have excelled on the back of Fami Ijeboi, a Minnesota transfer who has run 40 times for 260 yards over the last two weeks. QB Ryan Brown has shown growth, already matching last year's 9 TD passes, but doing it against a single Int after tossing 10 of them a year ago. The Husky defense absolutely must revert to their early-season form and leave last week's missed tackles and assignments in the rearview.

Of course, the more interesting question is what UW's offense will look like. While Purdue's defense has got the job done thus far in conference play, they still rank only 104th nationally in defensive SP+. Notre Dame, UCLA, and Wake Forest averaged over 40 ppg against them in their three losses. Washington's rush offense has been DOA most of the year with sub-par blocking and RB depth that was never supposed to be forced into regular action this year. However, Demond Williams' rib injury last week brough Elijah Brown in at QB and he immediately showed better timing and an ability to read the defense that brought the passing game to life. Was Brown's success a mirage against an Iowa defense that let its foot off the pedal with a big lead? Will he backslide against a defense that spent the week preparing for him? Above all, Brown has to play within himself and avoid turnovers. Purdue has surged by avoiding turnovers and UW doesn't have enough margin for error to lose the turnover differential. Maybe I'm just looking at this game through rose-colored glasses because I can't imagine UW losing out and this looks like the best chance to win a B1G game, but I feel relatively optimistic this week.

Indiana's winning streak very nearly came to a halt last week against Nebraska. They escaped, but the task ahead only gets tougher. Despite their season-opening loss in Austin, Ohio St is #1 in the country by SP+ (for their part, Indiana is 5th). Ohio St has defended the run very well this year, which could force Josh Hoover to do more against a great secondary than he has had to do most of the year. A big theme of Indiana's win last season in the B1G Championship Game was the pass rush, and Ohio St has questions about their own OL health. The game should be close, so I'm going to side with Jeremiah Smith, the best player in the country.

Northwestern has been one of the best stories of the season so far, at 4-1 with their only loss a close one to Indiana. Pat Fitzgerald will face Northwestern as a HC for the first time, and Aidan Chiles will start at QB for the Cats after going in the opposite direction. Northwestern runs the ball well, especially with RB Caleb Komolafe, while the Spartans do not defend it well. Michigan St will likely be able to move the ball and whether the game stays close will depend on whether Northwestern can force negative plays and red zone stops as they have all year.

The amazing thing about this game is that somebody has to win. Michigan has lost their last two (and would be 2-3 but for that wild ending to open the year against Western Michigan). Penn St has dropped three in a row and does not look ready to compete in the B1G. Michigan's struggles have bee mostly isolated to the offensive side and their run defense has been legitimately good. Penn St likes to play offense in a phone booth, so this game could get ugly. Michigan turns the ball over too much and struggles to pass consistently. The game should be low-scoring, which makes me lean toward the underdog.

Dylan Raiola probably didn't expect to start this game when he transferred from Nebraska to Oregon. However, he probably had that expectation because he thought he'd be backing up Dante Moore, not because he'd be coming off his worst game of the season (6/19, 43 yards, 3 turnovers). There is no confirmation yet, but it sounds like Brock Thomas is more likely to get the first crack. Nebraska's defense has been consistently solid under Matt Ruhle. The offense has generally looked better this year with OC Dana Holgerson and QB Anthony Colandrea. Even coming off a home loss, I think Autzen gives the Ducks an edge, but this game could go either way.

Even at 4-1, there is reason to remain skeptical of the Badgers. Their win over Penn St looks less impressive than it did at the time, and the rest of their victories have been against softer parts of the schedule. UCLA lost QB Nico Iamaleava for the year during the Oregon game and will likely use Ty Dieffnbach in his place. Regardless of who plays QB, Bob Chesney prefers to run the ball and the Bruins have done that well. Wisconsin is good against the run, but I'm not sure they're good enough to stymie Wayne Knight and company. UCLA leads then nation in takeaways and Wisconsin QB Colton Joseph has already thrown 5 picks. If Wisconsin can be neutral or better in turnovers, they can keep it close, but that might be asking a lot.

articles.title: Led by Angel Reese, six WNBA Finals competitors headline the 2026 All-Defensive First and Second Teams
articles.summary: Both the Dream and Valkyries put three players on the 2026 All-Defensive Teams.
articles.body:
If there needed to be more evidence that defense will define these WNBA Finals, the 2026 WNBA All-Defensive Teams provided it, as three members of the Atlanta Dream and three members of the Golden State Valkyries combined to claim six of the 10 spots.

Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese headlines the All-Defensive First Team, where she is joined by Dream teammate Rhyne Howard. Jordin Canada was elected to the Second Team.

Gabby Williams, the Defensive Player of the Year runner up, secured a spot on the First Team, and two Valkyries, Veronica Burton and Kiah Stokes, represent Golden State on the Second Team.

The All-Defensive selection is a first for Reese. Both Howard and Burton earn their second-straight and second-overall defensive honors, while Stokes, after a more than decade gap, receives her second All-Defensive nomination, with her first earned in 2015 as member of the New York Liberty. Williams and Canada are now three-time All-Defensive honorees. Williams, then with the Seattle Storm, was awarded in 2022 and 2025; Canada got the nods in 2019 with the Storm and in 2023 with the Los Angeles Sparks.

Filling out the First Team alongside Reese, Howard and Williams were the Las Vegas Aces' A'ja Wilson and Washington Mystics' Shakira Austin. It's the sixth All-Defensive selection for the three-time Defensive Player of the Year Wilson, whereas Austin is a first-time nominee.

Austin's Mystics teammate, Sonia Citron, also earned her first All-Defensive award as a member of the Second Team. Rounding out the Second Team of Canada, Burton, Stokes and Citron is Breanna Stewart, with this marking the eighth All-Defensive award for the Liberty stalwart.

articles.title: Texas’ Arch Manning Urged to Make Bold Indiana Move Amid Heisman Talk
articles.summary: One analyst believes a change in offensive systems could completely change Manning's future, pointing to Indiana's success with transfer quarterbacks. The po...
articles.body:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning entered the season facing enormous expectations, but another uneven stretch from the Longhorns has raised questions about whether the offense is getting the most out of him.

Following Saturday's 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, Manning has thrown 10 touchdowns and five interceptions through five games. Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian has defended his quarterback, although the problems haven't been limited to Manning's mistakes.

Now, one college football analyst believes what may need to happen for the former five-star quarterback to reach his full potential is to make a transfer.

RJ Young Predicts Arch Manning Heisman Win at Indiana

FOX Sports' RJ Young argued that the responsibility for Texas' offensive struggles belongs more to its head coach than its quarterback.

"Texas doesn't have an Arch Manning problem. It has a Steve Sarkisian play-calling problem," Young wrote.

He then made a bold prediction about what Manning might accomplish in a different offense.

"Arch wins the Heisman Trophy if transfers to Indiana in 2027," Young wrote.

To be clear, Young wasn't suggesting that a transfer is in motion. There has been no reported decision by Manning to enter the portal, and nothing indicating Indiana is recruiting him. The comment was a what-if about the impact of coaching and offensive structure.

Young's example was Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover, who transferred from TCU following the 2025 season. The numbers behind his point are compelling.

"Josh Hoover threw 33 INTs in 35 games at TCU. At IU, he's rocking 17 TDs and 0 picks on the stat sheet," Young wrote.

Hoover has thrown for 1,364 yards with 17 touchdowns and no interceptions through six games, helping Indiana start 6-0. Across his final three seasons at TCU, he threw 33 interceptions in 35 appearances.

The comparison doesn't guarantee Manning would have the same results. But it does provide a reason to wonder what he might look like playing for Curt Cignetti.

Indiana's Quarterback Success Adds Intrigue to Arch Manning Idea

Cignetti has already helped one transfer quarterback reach the sport's highest individual honor. Fernando Mendoza arrived from California, won the 2025 Heisman Trophy and led Indiana to a 16-0 national championship season.

Hoover has kept the Hoosiers rolling in 2026, and his improvement in protecting the football only strengthens Young's argument about the coaching environment. Indiana has found a way to get strong production from two quarterbacks with vastly different backgrounds.

Texas, meanwhile, is coming off a loss in which Manning threw for 260 yards and three touchdowns but also had two fourth-quarter interceptions. The Longhorns fell from No. 1 to No. 7 in the AP poll, putting more attention on an offense that hasn't consistently met expectations.

Sarkisian has defended Manning against criticism tied to his famous last name, arguing that his successes deserve more recognition. Young's view goes further by questioning the play-calling around him.

Of course, Manning still has the rest of 2026 to work through those issues at Texas, and his plans for 2027 remain unknown. A move to Indiana would require several decisions that haven't been made.

That's what makes Young's prediction interesting rather than actionable: It's a statement about what Indiana's quarterback development might do for Manning, not evidence that he'll ever wear a Hoosiers uniform.

articles.title: Dave Roberts, Blake Snell lose after 7th-inning collapse
articles.summary: Blake Snell was dominating Game 3 of the NLCS. Until he wasn’t.
articles.body:
It's a tale as old as time: An All-Star left-handed starter for the Los Angeles Dodgers is dominating in a playoff start until it gets to the 7th inning. He throws a lot of pitches, maybe gets a little tired, and meanwhile Dave Roberts or Don Mattingly leaves him until disaster strikes.

Usually, that pitcher is Clayton Kershaw . Now that Kershaw has retired to focus on broadcasting a reclaiming the symbol of the rainbow, the burden of being Roberts' victim has fallen on one-year San Francisco Giants sensation Blake Snell.

In the 7th inning of the Dodgers' 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers, Snell was cruising along through six innings. After giving up a home run to Jackson Chourio on the first pitch of the game, Snell gave up only one more hit in the next six innings, retiring 14 Brewers in a row at one point. Then he walked Andrew Vaughn on seven pitches. Then, Jake Bauers started fouling pitches off.

Bauers fought off five two-strike pitches before going deep on Snell's 11th pitch of the at-bat, giving the Brewers a 3-2 advantage.

That took Snell's pitch count to 99. Though Snell is notorious for not going deep into games, Roberts chose to keep him in to face the left-handed Garrett Mitchell, even though a lefty had just taken Snell deep. It took only two more pitches for Roberts to regret his inaction.

It was immediately reminiscent of the 2019 Division Series between the Dodgers and Washington Nationals, when Kershaw came out of the bullpen and gave up back-to-back homers to Anthony Rendon and Juan Soto, the second another lefty-on-lefty matchup.

The common thread is that Roberts simply doesn't trust his bullpen in October a lot of the time. He may have been right to, since relievers Rory Sasaki and Justin Wrobleski let two more runs score in the 8th and 9th innings. Last season, Roberts got through a rough start by Shohei Ohtani in Game 7 of the World Series by using four starting pitchers in relief, including Snell, with Wrobleski the only full-time reliever entering the game.

Snell had some control issues in his first playoff start, walking five Atlanta Braves in 3.2 innings, though he only gave up one run. With the Dodgers trailing 3-0 in the series, he and Roberts may not get a chance to redeem themselves before the 2027 season.

Note: Snell may be in his second season pitching for the Dodgers, but the Giants still had to pay him $17M this year thanks to a deferred signing bonus from his 2024 contract. Maybe that's the reason he collapsed in the biggest moment. Simply getting a check from the 2026 Giants is enough to taint anyone in baseball with their 97-loss stink.

articles.title: Seahawks elevate pair of newcomers from practice squad for Broncos game
articles.summary: The special teams gunner is set to make his debut with Seattle.
articles.body:
Through the first month of the season, the Seattle Seahawks struggled with kickoff coverage and rank near the bottom of the league in yards allowed per return, but they're set to gain a key special teams asset ahead of a crucial Week 6 road matchup against the Denver Broncos.

The team announced they've elevated wide receiver and special teams gunner Irv Charles, as well as linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo from the practice squad. Both will make their team debuts.

Acquired from the New York Jets in May , Charles missed the first five games while on injured reserve with a knee issue but was designated to return to practice on October 7. Seattle activated him to the active roster on Tuesday , although, he was released a day later to make room for running back Velus Jones Jr . As a vested veteran, Charles wasn't subject to waivers and rerouted to the practice squad.

Upon his return, Charles is expected to play a key role on kick and punt returns—areas where he's highly regarded.

On the defensive side, Ciarlo's elevation was expected given the Seahawks will be without starting linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) and Chazz Surratt (chest), leaving a thin group even thinner.

The third year linebacker went undrafted out of Army in 2024 before signing with the Jets, but missed his entire rookie season with a knee injury. He was released in May, 2025 and spent time with the Buffalo Bills, Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans prior to signing with the Seahawks on September 30.

articles.title: Móstoles celebra su gran fiesta del deporte en su año más europeo
articles.standfirst: Móstoles vivió una jornada especial con la gira Patrimonio del Deporte de Radio MARCA, una programación dedicada al deporte local y una gran gala que reunió a destacadas figuras del deporte español.
articles.summary: Móstoles vivió una jornada especial con la gira Patrimonio del Deporte de Radio MARCA, una programación dedicada al deporte local y una gran gala que reunió a destacadas figuras del deporte español.
articles.body: Móstoles vivió una jornada muy especial con la llegada de la gira Patrimonio del Deporte de Radio MARCA, que se sumó a las celebraciones de la ciudad como Ciudad Europea del Deporte 2026. La localidad madrileña se convirtió durante todo el día en protagonista de la radio deportiva, con una programación especial dedicada a poner en valor su historia y reconocer a cuatro de sus grandes referentes: Raúl Campos ‘Chorry’, Rafa Martínez, Eva Manguán y María Varo. El gran colofón de la jornada fue la Gala del Deporte de Móstoles 2026, celebrada en el Teatro del Bosque, que reunió a destacadas figuras del deporte nacional y local. Entre los nombres reconocidos estuvieron Coral Bistuer, Eva Moral, Luis Milla, Javier Castillejo, Juan Antonio Corbalán y José Javier Hombrados, protagonistas de algunas de las grandes páginas de la historia del deporte español. Dentro de la jornada de Patrimonio del Deporte, Radio MARCA trasladó hasta Móstoles algunos de sus principales programas. La Pizarra de Quintana, de 10 a 13 horas, se emitió desde el IES Felipe Trigo, mientras que El Programa de Ortega tomó el relevo por la tarde desde el Teatro del Bosque, escenario también de la gala. Uno de los momentos más especiales de la jornada llegó con la entrega de los Premios Patrimonio del Deporte de Radio MARCA, que reconocieron a cuatro grandes referentes del deporte mostoleño. Raúl Campos ‘Chorry’, campeón de Europa de fútbol sala con España en 2016 y 136 veces internacional; María Varo, deportista del Tri Infinity Móstoles, campeona de Europa de duatlón en 2025 y cuatro veces consecutivas campeona de España; Rafa Martínez, campeón de Europa de gimnasia artística en 2005 y 2007; y Eva Manguán, leyenda del fútbol sala femenino y elegida mejor jugadora del mundo en 2007. Por la tarde llegó el gran colofón con la Gala del Deporte de Móstoles 2026,Entre las figuras distinguidas estuvieron Eva Moral, medallista paralímpica de bronce en triatlón en Tokio; y Coral Bistuer, una de las grandes pioneras del taekwondo español, campeona del mundo y de Europa, además de medallista olímpica en Barcelona 1992. También recibieron reconocimiento Luis Milla, campeón de Liga con el Barcelona y el Real Madrid y campeón de Europa sub-21 como seleccionador; Javier Castillejo, campeón del mundo de boxeo en dos categorías; Juan Antonio Corbalán, medalla de plata en los Juegos de Los Ángeles 1984; y José Javier Hombrados, campeón del mundo de balonmano y medallista olímpico. La gala sirvió además para reconocer el esfuerzo, la dedicación y los éxitos de los deportistas y clubes de Móstoles, verdaderos protagonistas de una ciudad que ha hecho del deporte una de sus principales señas de identidad. Entre los galardonados destacaron Sergio Ibáñez Bañón y Almudena Álvarez de la Puente, premiados por sus trayectorias deportivas; el Club AGAD Móstoles y el Club Baloncesto Ciudad de Móstoles, por su labor en el fomento del deporte base; y la Asociación para la Práctica del Judo Móstoles, por su impulso al deporte inclusivo. También se reconoció la labor de Protección Civil y se rindió homenaje a los clubes históricos de la ciudad.Una noche de emociones y reconocimientos que reafirmó el compromiso de Móstoles con el deporte y dejó patente el orgullo de una ciudad que vive y siente el deporte.

articles.title: Texas A&M baseball releases complete 2027 schedule
articles.summary: Texas A&M’s 2027 schedule features five home SEC series, the BRUCE BOLT College Classic and a road series against Texas.
articles.body:
Texas A&M baseball released its complete 2027 schedule Wednesday, giving fans their first look at the path Michael Earley's team will face during his third season in College Station.

The Aggies will open the season with a three-game series at Blue Bell Park from Feb. 19-21. Their early nonconference schedule includes several home games before they travel to Houston for the BRUCE BOLT College Classic at Daikin Park. A&M will face Louisville on March 5, Louisiana on March 6 and Houston on March 7. The Aggies then return home for a midweek game and a three-game series against Loyola Marymount before opening SEC play.

Texas A&M begins its conference schedule at Alabama from March 19-21. The Aggies' five home SEC series will come against Tennessee, Oklahoma, LSU, Arkansas and Ole Miss.

The Oklahoma series should be one of the most anticipated weekends at Blue Bell Park. The Sooners are the defending national champions and haven't played in College Station since the programs were in the Big 12. A&M's conference road schedule includes trips to Alabama, Kentucky, Mississippi State, South Carolina and Texas. The Lone Star Showdown will be played May 14-16 in Austin before the Aggies close the regular season against Ole Miss from May 20-22.

The SEC Tournament is scheduled for May 25-30 at Hoover Metropolitan Stadium in Alabama.

The schedule will test a roster featuring 29 newcomers and only 15 returning letterwinners. Earley also enters the season with a new pitching coach in Barry Enright and associate head coach Nolan Cain back in College Station. Fall exhibitions against Rice and McNeese give the staff its first opportunities to evaluate the rebuilt roster before the Aggies begin their 2027 season in February.

Contact/Follow us @AggiesWire on X and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Texas A&M news, notes, and opinions. Follow Jarrett Johnson on X: @whosnextsports1 .

articles.title: Angel Reese, Gabby Williams headline WNBA All-Defensive team: Full list
articles.summary: The 2026 WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will feature six of the 10 players named to the WNBA All-Defensive teams.
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will feature six of 10 players named to the WNBA All-Defensive teams. Yes, you read that right.

Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese followed up her 2026 Defensive Player of the Year award with first-team All-Defensive honors, the WNBA announced on Thursday, Oct. 15. Reese is joined by Dream teammates Rhyne Howard and Jordin Canada, who earned first and second team honors, respectively.

The Dream's trio of defensive superstars will go head-to-head in the WNBA Finals against the Valkyries, who have their own trio of All-Defensive players. Valkyries forward Gabby Williams , who finished second in DPOY voting behind Reese, was named to the first team for the second consecutive season. Guard Veronica Burton and center Kiah Stokes were named to the second team.

Here are the WNBA players named to the 2026 WNBA All-Defensive teams:

Liberty, Dream and Aces, Valkyries in WNBA semifinal playoff action

Washington Mystics C Shakira Austin : The 6-foot-5 center anchored the league's top rebounding team, with the Mystics averaging 37.7 rebounds per game. Austin ranked second in the league in defensive rebounds (7.6) and fourth in total rebounds (9.5). She joins A'ja Wilson and Jonquel Jones as the only three players to average at least nine rebounds and one block this season.

Atlanta Dream G Rhyne Howard : The 6-foot-2 guard led the league in steals per game (2.3), setting a Dream single-season record (99) for steals in the process. Howard recorded three or more steals in 19 games this season, including two six-steal outings. Howard ranked third in the league in defensive win shares (3.2).

Atlanta Dream F Angel Reese : Reese, the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year , picked up her first All-Defensive nod. The 6-foot-4 forward led the league in rebounds (12.1), offensive rebounds per game (4.8) and defensive win shares (3.4), while setting WNBA single-season records for total rebounds (521), total offensive rebounds (206) and double-doubles (32). Reese averaged a career-high 1.8 steals per game, which ranked third in the league behind Dream teammates Howard and Canada (1.9).

Golden State Valkyries F Gabby Williams : The 5-foot-11 forward finished second in DPOY voting for the second consecutive season after ranking second in the league in defensive NET points (25) and fifth in steals per game (1.6). The 2025 first-team All-Defensive pick has recorded three or more steals in eight games this season. Williams, who played for France, was named the Best Defensive Player at the FIBA Women's World Cup.

Las Vegas Aces C A'ja Wilson : The 6-foot-4 center was named All-Defense for the seventh season straight. Wilson led the league in total blocks (79), blocks per game (1.9) and steals and blocks per game (3.3). She recorded a season-high five blocks in the Aces' 79-69 win over the Los Angeles Sparks on June 2, where she added 25 points and 15 rebounds to her stat line. The 2026 WNBA MVP has recorded three or more blocks in 10 games this season and grabbed 15 rebounds in five games. She finished third in the league in defensive rebounds (7.5) and fifth in rebounds per game (9.4).

Golden State Valkyries G Veronica Burton : The 5-foot-9 guard led the league in defensive win shares (.212) and defensive NET points (29), all while averaging a career-high 1.6 steals per game, which is tied for fifth in the league. It marks Burton's second consecutive WNBA All-Defensive second-team honor.

Golden State Valkyries C Kiah Stokes : The 6-foot-3 center ranked second in the league in total blocks (74) and fourth in the league in blocks per game (1.7). Stokes recorded three or more blocks in 11 games this season and five or more blocks in three contests. She had season-high seven blocks in the Valkyries' win over the Atlanta Dream on June 26.

Washington Mystics G Sonia Citron : The 6-foot-1 guard averaged 1.2 steals and 0.6 blocks in her sophomore season. She recorded three games with three or more steals, including a five-steal outing in the Mystics' win over the New York Liberty on June 19. She also had five games this season with two or more blocks. Citron became the first guard in franchise history to record 150 rebounds, 45 steals and 25 blocks in a single season.

Atlanta Dream G Jordin Canada : The 5-foot-6 guard finished second in the league with 1.9 steals per game, finishing behind her Dream teammate Rhyne Howard. Canada recorded 14 games this season with three or more steals, including a season-high seven steals in the Dream's loss to the Las Vegas Aces on May 17.

New York Liberty F Breanna Stewart : The 2026 WNBA Commissioner's Cup MVP is leading the Liberty in points (19.2), steals (1.4) and blocks (1.3) in her 10th season in the league, while ranking second in rebounds (8.5). Stewart has scored double-digits in all but one game this season and her seven double-doubles is tied for the fifth-most in the league. Stewart has been named All-Defense eight times.

articles.title: ‘Loyal to your soil’: Fans celebrate Sacramento Kings at annual Fan Fest
articles.summary: (FOX40.COM) — Grab your snacks, your dancing shoes and your Sacramento spirit, because Wednesday night at the Golden 1 Center, fans across the region joined...
articles.body:
(FOX40.COM) -- Grab your snacks, your dancing shoes and your Sacramento spirit, because Wednesday night at the Golden 1 Center, fans across the region joined together for the Sacramento Kings' annual Fan Fest and open practice.

While many community members were there to celebrate basketball, this special event puts the fans in the spotlight.

"I haven't been to a Kings game in years," a fan, James, said. "I want to come figure out who the new team is now."

Seas of purple took over the night as fans united under one roof to showcase their pride and dedication.

"You have to be loyal to your soil," one fan told FOX40. "You're in Sacramento. You've got to represent your city. You've got to stay loyal no matter what -- light the beam!"

FOX40 asked fans what they are most excited for this season and what they love most about the Kings and Fan Fest.

"The game," one fan said. "Zach LaVine, the game ... definitely the game. The excitement for the city, the game, the amazing dancers. It's just always lit. It's a good time."

"My favorite thing about the Sacramento Kings is when we light the beam," another fan screamed out.

Some fans said other elements of the team stood out the most.

"The color purple," one fan said when asked what she loves most about the team.

And for James, the sport itself is the focal point of Wednesday's event.

"Basketball, I love basketball," James said regarding his loyalty to the team.

"I'm excited to see everybody play, all the new players [to begin]," a fan named Susan said alongside her family. "We want to see the dance off, gotta love it, them dancing. I want to see what the new players' moves are."

From names on jerseys to entertainment on the courts, this fan fest was about supporting your team.

Fans like Ryder Gillespie said the Kings have a special place in their hearts.

"I've kind of started picking up basketball because of the Kings," Gillespie said. "It's been great. I've been a fan ever since I was a kid, so, I come out here every year and it's just really fun."

Some fans are new, others have been here since before Slamson and the color purple.

"If you're going to be true, be true to it," James said. "I was here since ARCO, so I've been a fan for that many years."

Attendees enjoyed free snacks, discounted merch and a chance to support Sutter Health patients, all while smiling with one another and building up their anticipation for the new season ahead.

"The fans are great," Gillespie said. "It's great out here. I love all the new faces, everything."

The Kings first regular season game against the Los Angeles Clippers kicks off next Wednesday.

articles.title: Stayton football forfeits game with rival Cascade
articles.summary: Stayton football has forfeited its Week 7 game against Cascade. It's another in a growing trend in Oregon high school football.
articles.body:
Another Oregon high school football team has forfeited a varsity game.

On Oct. 15, just a day before kickoff against rival Cascade in Turner, Stayton has forfeited the Week 7 conference game.

"The contest was forfeited because a team did not have enough participants in order to play. The team forfeited prior to competition; the contest was never started. Forfeit posted by OSAA on 10/15/2026," reads a message on the Oregon School Activities Association scoreboard.

The Statesman Journal reached out to Stayton High School but was unable to reach the principal, athletic director or football coach for comment.

Cascade, the reigning 4A state champion, loses a matchup with one of its biggest rivals in the heart of the season.

"We got word yesterday that they were concerned about their roster and the health of their roster, so there was communication between superintendents about that," Cascade athletic director and football coach Shane Hedrick said Oct. 15. "Today they called and said due to those concerns, they'd be withdrawing their teams for both varsity and JV."

The varsity game between the two schools was scheduled for Oct. 16 and the junior varsity game for Oct. 19.

"We totally understand the safety of the game and respect that," Hedrick added. "This game is so strong in this community in this era. And it's senior night for us ... but the underlying thing is that the game has to be safe, we totally agree to that."

According to the OSAA website, the Eagles have 35 players on the varsity roster. Prior to this week, the Eagles were on a two-game losing streak but hold a 3-3 overall record and Class 4A's No. 21 overall ranking.

Stayton is not the first Willamette Valley football team to have cancelled a game, or season, this fall. Back in early September, 3A's Blanchet Catholic cancelled its varsity season due to low numbers after two games.

Down Interstate 5, 5A school South Eugene cancelled its varsity season nearly a week before opening kickoff.

In the same conference as Stayton and Cascade this week, a game between Central/Kings Valley Charter and Gladstone/Riverdale was forfeited due to "not enough participants in order to play," according to the OSAA.

Gladstone/Riverdale has also already forfeited its Week 9 game against Cascade, Hedrick said.

Cascade's next scheduled varsity game is Oct. 23 at home against McKay. Stayton's varsity team is scheduled to host Philomath on Oct. 23.

There have been several more one-game forfeits and season cancellations across Oregon this fall. It's a growing trend that's now reached into Class 4A's Special District 2.

Landon Bartlett covers high school sports and Oregon State for the Statesman Journal. He can be reached at LBartlett@statesmanjournal.com or on X, TikTok or Instagram @bartlelo.

articles.title: Former Cleveland Browns WR David Bell seeks $300M after botched surgery allegedly nearly killed him
articles.summary: David Bell claims Dr. William Meyers cut his femoral artery during a sports hernia repair, ending his NFL career and prompting a $300 million lawsuit.
articles.body: Former Cleveland Browns wide receiver David Bell is suing well-known surgeon Dr. William Meyers, Jefferson Health, and 14 other parties for more than $300 million. Bell claims an unnecessary surgery nearly cost him his life and forced him to walk away from the NFL at just 24 years old. The trouble started after Bell hurt his hip during Week 2 of the 2024 season. According to the lawsuit filed in Philadelphia, doctors used misleading scan results to convince him he needed core muscle surgery, commonly known as a sports hernia repair, that he never actually required. The complaint claims this was part of a profit-driven pattern of pushing pro athletes into procedures they did not need. DOJ CHARGES 19 DEFENDANTS IN ALLEGED $4M PHILADELPHIA MEDICARE AND MEDICAID FRAUD Things went wrong on the operating table. The lawsuit alleges that Dr. Meyers cut Bell's femoral artery, the main artery supplying blood to the leg, causing massive internal bleeding. The clinic was not equipped to handle that kind of emergency, so Bell was rushed by ambulance to Thomas Jefferson Hospital. Doctors there performed urgent surgery to repair the artery and save his leg, but the ordeal left him with lasting physical damage. SUPREME COURT HANDS NFL A LOSS IN BRIAN FLORES DISCRIMINATION LAWSUIT, CLEARING PATH TO TRIAL Before the injury, Bell was a reliable target in Cleveland's offense. The Browns drafted the former Big Ten Receiver of the Year out of Purdue in the third round back in 2022. articles.body: South Korean running influencer Yoo Ji-won, 25, died after collapsing just 500 metres from the finish line of the Seoul Race half-marathon on October 11, 2026. She was rushed to a medical facility after the incident but could not be saved, according to the race organisers. Ji-won was also an artificial intelligence semiconductor researcher at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST). She had built a following of more than 8,000 people on Instagram by sharing her running journey and race results. The cause of her death has not been publicly confirmed.Yoo Ji-won was a KAIST researcher who shared her running journey onlineYoo Ji-won balanced her work in science with her passion for running. She researched artificial intelligence semiconductors at KAIST while sharing her training sessions and race performances with her Instagram followers.Her account, under the handle @mta1n_0ne, had attracted more than 8,000 followers. She regularly posted about her runs, giving people a look at her progress and achievements in the sport.Her final Instagram post, shared on October 4, showed her timing from a 10-kilometre run. Following news of her death, the post became a place for friends and followers to share their condolences and remember her.According to South Korean media reports, Ji-won had also achieved strong results in local races. She won the women’s masters 10-kilometre category at the Gunsan Saemangeum Marathon in April 2026. She had also completed the full Seoul Marathon in March, finishing in two hours, 56 minutes and 32 seconds, according to the International Business Times UK.Yoo Ji-won collapsed at 20.6km as Seoul Race organisers confirm deathThe incident happened at around 8:49 am on October 11 during the 2026 Seoul Race half-marathon. After providing emergency first aid at the scene, the individual was transported to a medical facility via a 119 ambulance for treatment; however, sadly, the participant passed away.“We offer our deepest condolences to the bereaved family facing this sudden tragedy and pray for the repose of the soul of the deceased. The Organizing Committee will closely examine the matter and take necessary follow-up measures,”The organisers said they would review what happened and take the necessary follow-up measures. However, they did not announce a cause of death. As soon as I crossed the finish line, I looked for you on the awards podium, but then came the unsettling news, and I began to sense a reality I didn’t want to believe,” Bummy wrote.His account reflected the shock of learning that a fellow runner had died during an event where participants had gathered to complete their races. articles.title: LB Donovan Robinson Has Chance to Make Impact for Washington Football
articles.summary: With starter Xe'ree Alexander set to miss time with an injury, another young Husky has a chance to make an impact come Friday night.
articles.body:
Coming off the worst showing of defensive coordinator Ryan Walters' career against Iowa, Washington's defense is looking to bounce back this week against a Purdue offense that just hung up 41 points on Minnesota. As the Huskies continue to battle the injury bug, another key player has fallen victim: fourth-year linebacker Xe'ree Alexander.

While the unit has plenty of depth to maintain a high level of play, the absence of Alexander opens the door for another promising young talent.

In comes second-year player Donovan Robinson Jr., who, after redshirting his freshman season, put on an impressive showing in fall camp. Listed at 6-foot-2 and 225 pounds, the second-year player presents both the size and athleticism to be an impact player in the Big Ten, but has struggled to find playing time in Walters' core rotation behind the injured Alexander, fifth-year seniors Jacob Manu and Tariq Al-Uqdah, and sophomore Zaydrius Rainey-Sale.

Despite the lack of experience, defensive coordinator Ryan Walters has a lot of confidence in the former three-star recruit, who could see a major increase in action.

"Donnie has done a great job in his growth and his improvement," Walters said on Tuesday. "He's made a ton of plays on special teams, and he continues to get better defensively, and if his number's called, I've got full faith and confidence, and so does the defense, in him."

Through the first half of the season, Robinson has racked up 6 tackles, most of which have come on special teams. After redshirting his first season on Montlake, the product of Loyola Academy High School in the greater Chicago area emerged this offseason as a player who could play a major role in the defense moving forward. Although those opportunities haven't necessarily come just yet, the door will be open to put out quality tape on Friday night against Purdue.

With their backs against the wall facing off against a formidable opponent on the road, Washington has no other choice but to continue to rely on their young talent to come up with winning plays, something that is yet to be seen in Big Ten play.

While the raw talent of Jedd Fisch's past two recruiting classes has been on full display this year, it hasn't directly correlated with wins. Robinson will have the opportunity to help change that narrative.

articles.body:
Cleveland Guardians closer Cade Smith delivered another dominant postseason performance Thursday, recording a four-out save in a 3-2 ALCS Game 3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays at Progressive Field.

Smith entered with the tying run on third and two outs in the eighth inning after Hunter Gaddis allowed a double. He struck out Yandy Diaz after a 10-pitch battle, then retired the Rays in order in the final frame. The outing gave Smith his second save of the postseason and helped the Guardians seize a 2-1 series lead.

MLB Network shared a postgame clip on X, formerly Twitter, of the All-Star closer discussing the Guardians' approach after securing the win.

Rookie Petey Halpin supplied the decisive offense with a two-run homer in the fifth, while Gavin Williams struck out nine over five innings. Cleveland's bullpen allowed only one baserunner across the final four frames.

articles.title: Caleb Williams – who felt ‘pop’ with hamstring injury – must pass ‘stress test’ to play vs. Falcons
articles.summary: LAKE FOREST, Ill. – Everything – this story and more about Caleb Williams – should start with the pop. It’s what Williams felt in his right hamstring when he...
articles.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. – Everything – this story and more about Caleb Williams – should start with the pop. It's what Williams felt in his right hamstring when he rolled to his left against the Minnesota Vikings and headed toward the end zone.

"That's why I looked back," Williams shared on Thursday. "I looked back just like everybody else does when you feel a pop. (You) think somebody grabbed you and nobody grabbed me."

And then down he went in Week 2 against the Vikings.

Williams needed help off the field and was later carted to the locker room. His placement on the cart itself and the emotions he showed – unfairly – resulted in an incessant amount of ridicule, particularly at the national level.

"I didn't know it wasn't going to be season ending," he said.

Williams would learn the severity of his hamstring injury the following Monday (Sept. 21) after an MRI. "It was a hamstring tear and a pretty serious one," he said.

As for the grade level of the tear, Williams will keep that to himself.

"Yeah, we got a grade," Williams said, "but I wouldn't say it's deserved to be put out there … after all the false ones."

It was apparent that Williams was unhappy with how his injury situation had been covered from the start.

"There's nothing that has come out that has been right about what it is and what it has been," Williams said as a part of a lengthy opening statement.

The initial coverage only fueled more ridicule of Williams.

"Yeah, I'm always going to show emotion, especially when I can't be out there with the guys when something like that happens," he said. "When I went through the draft process, I went to two places and the two places was here and (I) popped over to the Vikings for a visit as we all know. And they asked me what's the difference between you and everyone else? It's because I care about the team, about the organization, winning, being out there, my teammates, all of that. So I care – and that's the biggest thing. This is what I love to do. This puts a smile on my face. It's everything to me. So not being able to be out there was frustrating. That was more of the tears or whatever that was.

"And then the other half of it was just everybody making jokes and all of that, but that doesn't bother me. It's the other half of the national or the local and then putting out false things that weren't true, to then allow people to go and run with it. So, that's all right. We'll be back out here soon and we'll be ready to roll."

It wasn't new territory for Williams. But it was the first time he was dealing with a serious injury in the NFL.

"My character has been attacked … for a while," he said. "It's just another motivating factor when I get out there and get going again."

Williams was a full participant in practice on Thursday. But he opened his news conference at Halas Hall by saying that he doesn't know if he's playing Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta.

"(I) have to go through a bunch of medical protocols," he said. "I obviously have to get out there and practice – do the stress testing that obviously you do when you're trying to come back from injury or serious injury."

"It's data – loading it," Williams said. "Practice is loading it in many different positions just because you've got a (defensive) line rushing you, so you're putting your body in positions that you can't really replicate because it's more of a reaction in practice and game. You're putting yourself in those positions in practice and that's a stress test of being able to go through a whole week and see how it goes and then you get to the end of the week, you feel good and medical approves and strength and conditioning approves with my strength and the flexibility and all of that, all that good stuff that they all know, it's a team working together trying to get it right."

Everything Williams did at Lambeau Field before the game on Sunday also was a step – maybe quite a few – in the right direction for his return. His daily routine has included five to six hours of rehab work with Bears staff members. After that, he said he uses "a bunch of machines and things like that" to enhance his recovery while at home.

"I can move. I can run," Williams said. "I hit a top speed the other day, one of my high speeds I've ever hit. And so I can move, I can run. I've got strength. It's like I said, just going through the stress test because obviously fibers and things like that in your hamstrings and things like that in your hamstrings and muscles have to connect back together to be able to go out there and play a 60-minute game."

articles.title: Scotia-Glenville wins third straight Section 2 Class B girls' tennis title
articles.summary: Standout sisters Isabel and Gabby Amurao set the tone for Scotia-Glenville with identical 6-0, 6-0 wins, but the team's six new members all contributed to th...
articles.body:
SCHENECTADY - Of the nine Scotia-Glenville players who stepped onto the court at Central Park on Thursday afternoon for the Section 2 Class B girls' tennis championship match against Ichabod Crane, just three of them were members of the squad that captured the Tartans' second straight sectional championship in 2025.

On Thursday, the six newcomers also became champions.

Standout sisters Isabel and Gabby Amurao set the tone for top-seeded Scotia-Glenville with identical 6-0, 6-0 wins in the Nos. 1 and 2 singles matches, respectively, but the six new members of the team all contributed as well in a 6-1 victory to give the Tartans a Class B three-peat.

"It's really exciting," Isabel Amuaro said. "Especially because it's my last year as a senior, and this is our third sectional title for our team in a row. It's great that we were able to rebuild so fast, losing so many seniors last year and having such a different team this year and still doing great."

Scotia-Glenville (11-4 overall) coach Geoff Olson said the team had some growing pains early in the season as it integrated new players into the lineup, but the Tartans grew as the season went on.

Now, the team has a chance to equal or exceed last year's squad, which reached the semifinals of the Division 2 state tournament. The Tartans will face Class C/D champion Greenwich on Sunday at 1 p.m. at Central Park for the right to be Section 2's representative in the Division 2 regionals.

"It's our third year in a row, and we didn't see it coming, because we lost so many seniors last year," Scotia-Glenville coach Geoff Olson said. "We just reloaded, and the girls believed, and they came through. … The first week, we were like, 'OK, we've got some work to do,' but I'm telling you, it came together."

While Scotia-Glenville had to get contributions from its newcomers to top No. 2 seed Ichabod Crane and bring home the program's third straight sectional title, it was the Amurao sisters - the Tartans' two team captains - who led the way once again.

Both Isabel, a senior, and Gabby, a sophomore, have been on all three Tartans championship teams. On Thursday, Isabel Amurao won 6-0, 6-0 over Ichabod Crane's Libby Spensieri in the No. 1 singles match, while Gabby Amurao was a 6-0, 6-0 winner over Payge Cook in No. 2 singles.

"Having them up top always helps your team," Olson said.

The Amurao sisters face a busy week ahead. After they try to lead their team back to regionals this weekend, they'll both start the Section 2 singles tournament on Monday with strong prospects. Isabel Amurao, the runner-up in last year's sectional tournament behind eventual state champion Jolie Chichak of Shenendehowa, is the No. 2 seed behind Chichak, while Gabby Amurao is the No. 8 seed.

Though the individual tournament is still to come, for now the sisters are focused on their team's goals.

"It would be really fun," Gabby Amurao said, "if we could go (to states) again."

In addition to the wins by their captains, Scotia-Glenville got a 6-4, 6-0 win by Caroline Grainer over Ichabod Crane's Annie Lockmer in No. 3 singles, a 6-3, 6-4 win by Adelyn Cowdrey over Maddy Kaminski in No. 4 singles, a 6-4, 6-3 win by Sophia Lippiello and Lyla Jones over Ally DeMatteo and Lana Nelson in No. 1 doubles, and a 6-0, 6-2 win by Brooklyn House and Zoey McConnelee over Allorra Cirillo and Lily Stevens in No. 2 doubles.

Halo Schieren was the lone victor for the second-seeded Riders, notching a 6-2, 7-5 win over Scotia's Audra Zebrowski in the No. 5 singles match.

Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love might be on his way to missing his first game this season. Dealing with an ankle injury, he did not practice for the second day in a row on Thursday.

With two DNPs, it is becoming far less likely that Love will be able to play on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams .

He suffered a high ankle sprain in the preseason and recovered in time to play in Week 1, but that is not the ankle that is bothering him, and, per head coach Mike LaFleur, that ankle is perfectly recovered. It was his other ankle he tweaked at some point, and it has been lingering. The team has called his practice use and treatment in games as "maintenance" and "management," but it finally looks like he is going to miss time.

A recent roster move suggests Love won't be able to play at least this week.

They signed Jerome Ford to the practice squad. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are the only other running backs on the active roster and Evan Hull was on the practice squad. Signing Ford suggests that the Cardinals knew that Love wouldn't get any practice reps this week.

The question between now and Saturday, when the Cardinals will announce final roster moves for their game on Sunday, is whether or not Love will get placed on injured reserve. We can likely expect, at minimum, that Hull will be elevated to the active roster to play, with Allgeier and Knight handling the offensive load against the Rams.
