articles.title: The 49ers open the practice window for WR Christian Kirk
articles.summary: (AP) — The San Francisco 49ers opened the 21-day practice window for receiver Christian Kirk on Thursday, giving the team another possible option to bolster...
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — The San Francisco 49ers opened the 21-day practice window for receiver Christian Kirk on Thursday, giving the team another possible option to bolster an injury-filled position group.

Kirk practiced on a limited basis for the first time since hurting his calf in the first training camp practice in July. Kirk began the season on injured reserve and finally was able to get back on the field with his teammates after what coach Kyle Shanahan described as an "awesome weekend" in his recovery.

"Just felt like I kind of got over that hump and felt like myself again," Kirk said. "The body started to respond to the training and the recovery and whatnot. Just wanted to communicate that to them, and tell them that I was ready to go, and get back out there. So, excited to get out there. It's obviously been a while, and just ready to attack this week."

The move comes with the 49ers (5-0) missing injured receivers Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson for time already and now Deebo Samuel out for at least a few weeks after hurting his hamstring last weekend in Seattle. Shanahan said he doesn't expect Samuel back until the first game following the bye Nov. 8 at the earliest.

No. 1 receiver Mike Evans also has been dealing with two broken ribs and now has soreness in his Achilles that kept him out of practice.

The only healthy receivers at practice on the 53-man roster were Brandin Cooks, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing as the team prepares for a game Monday night against Washington before Kirk jumped right in.

"It's like riding a bike," he said. "I've been doing it for a while, and so, for me, it's just getting back out there, getting integrated with the guys. Obviously, it's been hard not being out there, but been really cool to watch day in and day out how this team comes to work every single day, and for it to be able to carry over on Sundays. I'm just excited to get in the mix, and hopefully, provide some production to help us win some more games."

Kirk signed a one-year, $3 million deal with San Francisco in free agency in March. The 29-year-old Kirk has 432 catches for 5,415 yards and 30 touchdowns in eight seasons with Arizona, Jacksonville and Houston.

He missed 18 games the past three seasons with Jacksonville and Houston with injuries to his groin, collarbone and hamstring and was frustrated to be dealing with another injury with his new team.

"Anytime you go to a new organization, a new team, no matter what you've done, you want to prove yourself, and that's just how I felt," Kirk said. "I've just wanted to go out there, obviously, play with these guys. ... But to just be able to get out there and prove to them that I'm worthy to be a teammate and to be able to help win football games here. For me, it's been hard, but it's all about just how you approach every day and control what you can control."

The 49ers made two other roster moves on Thursday, promoting defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo from the practice squad back to the active roster to fill a spot vacated by the one-game suspension of linebacker Dre Greenlaw. Linebacker Eugene Asante was signed to the practice squad for more depth at the position with Greenlaw and Garret Wallow (hamstring) out this week.

Defensive end Nick Bosa (calf) didn't practice Thursday, but Shanahan said there's a chance he could return this week after missing the past three games.

Defensive tackle Gracen Halton (quadriceps), James Thompson Jr. (ankle) and safety S Marques Sigle (ankle) also were out of practice.

Fullback Kyle Juszczyk was limited after missing last week's game with a knee injury. Right tackle Colton McKivitz (illness) and cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder) were also limited.

Tennessee holds a 5-1 record while Alabama sits at 5-1 after a narrow loss to Georgia. Both teams need a win to stay in the hunt for the SEC title.

The matchup features two teams that have dealt with recent struggles. Alabama lost 20-17 to Georgia at home in Week 6, while Tennessee has climbed the rankings after beating weaker opponents. Fans in Tuscaloosa are nervous about their coaching staff, but writer Dan Wolken says the evidence points to Kalen DeBoer staying long-term. The game takes place at Neyland Stadium, where the home crowd will be loud and the pressure high for both sides.

Alabama loses a key weapon in the passing game

The biggest story for the Crimson Tide is the absence of Ryan Coleman-Williams. In six games this season, he accumulated 415 receiving yards and four touchdowns. DeBoer confirmed on Monday that the receiver has a knee injury and a head issue that need attention. "Has got a couple things going on," DeBoer said. The coach added that the team will address the lower extremity issue this week but likely will not have him for the weekend.

Without Coleman-Williams, Alabama's offense must find new ways to move the ball. The receiver was one of the best options for the quarterback to target in tight spots. Losing him forces other players to step up immediately against a Tennessee defense that plays well at home. This injury changes the game plan and could slow down the passing attack significantly. The team has to work through this week to see if he can return for future games.

DeBoer also noted that the receiver might be "week-to-week" after this weekend. This means the team cannot count on him returning for the next few games either. The coaching staff must adjust their strategy to account for this loss. The depth chart will be tested, and young players will get more snaps than expected.

Tennessee holds the advantage with home crowd support

Tennessee enters the game with a 5-1 record and will host Alabama in Neyland Stadium, which is one of the toughest places to play in college football. The home team usually benefits from the noise and energy of the crowd. This factor could help the Volunteers make big plays on both sides of the ball.

Alabama, on the other hand, is coming off a loss to Georgia that dropped them to No. 6 in the rankings. The Crimson Tide were close to winning that game but fell short 20-17. Now they face a tough road test against a team that is confident and playing at home. The mood in Tuscaloosa is mixed, with some fans questioning the coaching staff. However, Wolken argues that DeBoer is the right choice for the long haul and that fans should accept it.

The coaching situation matters more than one game

Many Alabama fans want to move on from Kalen DeBoer because he is not Nick Saban. They feel he has not had great success yet and want a change. However, the evidence suggests he is the right fit for the program. During his second season, DeBoer guided Alabama to the playoffs with an 11-4 record. Although they were defeated by Georgia in the SEC title game, Oklahoma lost to them in the first round.

Wolken wrote that Alabama's leadership believes strongly in DeBoer and that he wants to stay for the long term. He remarked that no one realistically available for hire in college football could outperform Alabama's current options. "It's time for all Alabama fans and, frankly, the college football gossip machine to finally accept it: DeBoer and Alabama are a good match, and he's not going anywhere anytime soon," Wolken wrote. This is a reality check for fans who expect immediate perfection.

The loss to Georgia was close, and the team showed they can compete with the best. Now they face a rival team with a strong defense and a loud crowd. The coaching staff must prepare the team to handle the pressure of a big rivalry game. If they win, it proves the program is moving in the right direction. If they lose, it might fuel the criticism, but the long-term plan remains the same.

Three predictions for the Saturday showdown

First, Alabama will struggle to move the ball through the air without Coleman-Williams. The receiver's absence will force the quarterback to check down more often or hold the ball too long. Tennessee's defense will capitalize on these mistakes and create turnovers. The passing game will be limited, and the offense will rely too much on the running game.

Second, the home crowd at Neyland Stadium will play a major role in the outcome. The noise level will make it hard for Alabama to communicate on offense. Tennessee will use this to their advantage and score early. The crowd energy will keep the Volunteers in the game even if they fall behind.

Third, this will not change DeBoer's standing in Tuscaloosa. Sure, a win will quiet the noise after the Georgia loss, but as Wolken pointed out, Alabama's leadership firmly believes in DeBoer. A loss here would keep the critics and the media talking, but it will not drive him out. He is there to stay for the long haul.

articles.title: Banana Ball is coming to Notre Dame Stadium in 2027
articles.summary: Notre Dame Stadium will play host to a different type of sport than it normally does in 2027 when Banana Ball comes to town.
articles.body:
One of college football's most iconic venues is set to host a different sport in the summer of 2027.

The Savanah Bananas will be bringing its unique style of baseball to Notre Dame Stadium on Saturday, June 26, 2027, the organization announced on Thursday night .

Not only will they be bringing the traveling league and its six teams, but they will be debuting a new "360" version of the game. Two fields will be set up inside the stadium, with action alternating between the two, per a social media post.

"It's Banana Ball like you've never seen it before… 1 stadium, 1 game… 2 fields," the organization wrote in a social media post. "Banana Ball 360 brings the action to all 80,000 fans in South Bend. The field of play will alternate between two fields within Notre Dame Stadium to ensure that fans get the best seat in the house no matter where they sit."

What started as just the Savanah Bananas has grown into "Banana Ball," a six-team, world-traveling baseball league. Often compared to the Harlem Globetrotters in basketball, Banana Ball is as much about baseball as it is about entertainment. There are choreographed dance breaks, live music and more in a family-friendly environment.

Per another Facebook post from the company, Banana Ball was played in front of 4.3 million fans in 2026, visiting 23 MLB stadiums, 10 football stadiums and 73 cities total.

Ticket information for the visit to Notre Dame Stadium will be announced at a later date. Their schedule release also notes a June 24 date for Frank Eck Stadium, home to Notre Dame baseball. No details were announced on what the Banana Ball people will be doing on that date and location.

Notre Dame Stadium has opened its doors to more events beyond Notre Dame football games in the last decade. Multiple concerts have been held, including Luke Combs and AC/DC in 2026. An international soccer match featuring Liverpool was held in the summer of 2019, and the NHL's Winter Classic featured the Chicago Blackhawks and Boston Bruins on New Years Day 2019.

articles.title: Winnipeg Jets’ Lineup Uncertain Ahead Of Blackhawks Clash
articles.summary: The Winnipeg Jets face uncertainty as they gear up to face the Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday night as they seek to win two straight. The Jets will unfortuna...
articles.body:
The Winnipeg Jets face uncertainty as they gear up to face the Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday night as they seek to win two straight.

The Jets will unfortunately miss Josh Morrissey for the third straight game, so the defensive rotation must step up again. They did just that in Tuesday night's three-goal win over the Minnesota Wild. That must be the case again against Chicago.

Despite scoring five goals in their win over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Tuesday, the Hawks remain one of the league's most stagnant teams offensively. If the Jets' rotation holds and the forward groups provide help, likely starting goaltender Stuart Skinner should enjoy another great outing.

Skinner has a 3-0-1 record through four starts, a .750 quality starts percentage, a .917 save percentage, and a 2.47 GAA. Should Winnipeg keep stifling opponents in the second and third periods, Skinner should benefit.

Winnipeg Jets Projected Lines And Pairings Against Chicago

Besides Morrissey missing the action on Thursday night, Jets coach Scott Arniel faces another lineup decision.

This one is regarding Vlad Namestnikov. Per NHL.com , "Namestnikov is a game-time decision after he fell into the boards during the morning skate. If he can't play, Lambert will take his spot."

Namestnikov's status is one to watch as the late afternoon and evening hours tick by.

As for the projections, Kyle Connor, Mark Scheifele, and Cole Prefetti look like they will make up the first line. Nino Niederreiter, who the Jets brought back into the lineup on Tuesday night, appears to be keeping his spot on the second line with Viggo Björck and Gabriel Vilardi.

Isak Rosen looks like he's staying on the third line, with Adam Lowry and Alex Iafallo joining him. Namestnikov, Morgan Barron, and Cole Koepke are on the projected fourth line. But again, it's still wait-and-see with Namestnikov.

Mario Ferraro and Neal Pionk, and Dylan Samberg and Dylan DeMelo appear to be on the first two pairings. On Tuesday night , all four of them skated between 21:40 and 24:06. Last Friday, three of the four skated between 19:58 and 22:06, while Pionk skated for 25:02. Overall, these four have mostly been skating similar minutes.

For the third pairing, Hadyn Fleury is projected to line up alongside Jack St. Ivany. That likely leaves Tyrel Bauer as the scratch. Elias Salomonsson is on the mend but remains on the injured list. Meanwhile, Garrett Brown and Walker Duehr remain on injured reserve.

Jets' Lineup Uncertain In Upcoming Road Tilt

Despite uncertainties facing the Winnipeg Jets' lineup, the upside is that they are 2-0-0 on the road. Both wins came on a back-to-back against the Detroit Red Wings and Pittsburgh Penguins in 3-2 thrillers.

Given Winnipeg's track record so far on the road this season, the Jets should skate into Chicago and give the Blackhawks a hard time. That said, Winnipeg's defense must remain stingy while Kyle Connor, Cole Perfetti, and Co. go to work.

The Jets and Blackhawks will face off at 8:00 p.m. EDT in this early-season Central Division showdown.

articles.summary: Florida football has been exposed over the last two weeks, losing much of the trust it finally won back. A decisive victory over Ole Miss does not have nearl...
articles.body:
Florida football has been exposed over the last two weeks, losing much of the trust it finally won back. A decisive victory over Ole Miss does not have nearly as much cachet following back-to-back blowout losses to Missouri and South Carolina, the latter of which stunningly took place in The Swamp. The squad's early Playoff prospects have rapidly diminished, especially given what lies ahead, but all the Gators can do now is focus on Texas. Unfortunately, the Aaron Philo injury situation is forcing head coach Jon Sumrall to install a backup plan.

The starting quarterback, who transferred from Georgia Tech, is dealing with a shoulder injury and is questionable for Saturday's showdown in Austin, per On3's Pete Nakos. Wide receivers Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton join Philo in being game-time decisions versus the No. 7 Longhorns, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel.

Although Philo threw during Thursday's practice, Tramell Jones Jr. is getting ready to compete just in case the former is ruled out. It would be the redshirt freshman's first career college start, a potentially daunting scenario in the face of a ferocious Texas defense. Whoever is taking snaps at QB must be composed, because the home team is going to be in an unpleasant mood following last Saturday's Red River Rivalry loss to Oklahoma.

Though, the Gators should be plenty mad themselves. They failed to protect Ben Hill Griffin Stadium against a South Carolina squad that was bogged down in uncertainty entering the matchup. Jon Sumrall has not fixed all of the program's problems just yet .

Aaron Philo is aiming to reignite Florida football with a strong outing in The Lone Star State. He has completed an outstanding 70.5 percent of his passes for 1,341 yards and nine touchdowns, while rushing for 104 yards and another three scores. Sumrall will monitor his status and make a decision before the noon kickoff.

I have been sleuthing out the Tigers' schedule the past few weeks as other SEC teams released theirs and by using my best deductive reasoning skills, I had it allllllll figured out, except one week. [pats self on back approvingly]. On October 13, it was finally released, and now we can finally talk about it! **

In case you lived on another planet last year, let me remind you, the best team at the University of Missouri — it's true!! — entered the season with their highest preseason ranking in program history at no. 7, and finished the season ranked no. 11 (no. 8 in the regular season). The 2026 season, while you could ultimately say ended in disappointment— we want so much more for our favorite team!!! — featured first-time wins in Lexington and at Neville Arena, a program-best win over no. 2 Florida, and a trip to their sixth consecutive Regional Finals.

The Tigers' season-high score was a 197.55 earned in late February at the Mizzou Quad . They had a .500 record in the vaunted Southeastern Conference and finished 6-2 at home. Mizzou finished the season ranked 7th nationally on floor, 10th on vault and bars, and 11th on beam. If not for some beam wonkiness at season's end they would have been top 10 in all four apparatuses. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

The 2026 Tigers racked up a bunch of honors, including a SEC Specialist of the Year (for the third consecutive year) for Hannah Horton, WCGA Regular Season All-American honors for Addison Lawrence and Kimarra Echols, consecutive WCGA South Central Regional Coach of the Year awards for head coach Shannon Welker, a SEC Scholar Athlete of the Year for Lauren Macpherson, a WCGA Regional Assistant Coach of the Year for Jackie Terpak, a Regional title for Hannah, and an SEC-leading 10 All-SEC honors .

Anyway…. now that that's out of the way, more on the schedule.

The Tigers' unofficial start to the season will be the annual Black & Gold meet, which is (weirdly, in my eyes) much later than normal, and not scheduled until January 2 at 5pm. You can read how last year's meet went here .

To officially start the new season, the Tigers will ring in 2027 with an all-Big 10 matchup at Zou to the Lou on Friday, January 8, which makes its triumphant return after a year off and is the first of two podium meets scheduled during the regular season. This year's iteration will feature Illinois, Nebraska, and Iowa, and with it being during winter break (and at the Family Arena in St. Charles), I don't expect a massive crowd, as much as I'd love to see it.

IOWA ended the 2026 season ranked no. 17 nationally (no. 19 in the regular season) with a 196.473 NQS, 196.398 average, and 196.825 high score. Their best event was bars (no. 12), led by Aurelie Tran, who in September announced an achilles tear which will put her out of commission for the 2027 season. The Hawkeyes' weakest event was beam and floor (no. 24). Iowa's season ended in the second round of the Corvallis Regional (the so-called region of death) in what ended up being a very exciting matchup with Minnesota and UCLA for a trip to the Regional Final.

As for the last time Mizzou and Iowa matched up, it was the Zou to the Lou meet on Valentine's Day 2025 when Kennedy Griffin scored her first 10 on floor. The Tigers were victorious, scoring a 197.150 that beat Alabama (196.675), Illinois (196.225) and Iowa (195.00). NEBRASKA ended its season ranked no. 32 (no. 34 in regular season), with a 195.561 NQS, 195.589 average and 196.825 high score. The Cornhuskers made appearance in the second round of the Baton Rouge Regional. Floor was the weakest link for the Huskers in 2026 (no. 44), while bars was the best (no. 25). I recall Ms. Bowers cheering for Mizzou last season while sitting with the Wier Family; I guess that won't happen this year, huh?

ARKANSAS ended the season ranked no. 7 in the final polls (no. 9 in regular season) with a 197.170 NQS, 197.115 average, and 197.700 high score . The Gymbacks were strongest on vault and beam (no. 6), but just no. 16 on bars. Arky and Mizzou faced off a number of times head-to-head in 2026, with Mizzou taking the dual meet in the home finale (at Hearnes) by a score of 197.425 to 197.225, along with a head-to-head victory in the early session of the SEC Championships . Then, the Fightin Jordyn Wiebers got the best of the Tigers in both sessions of the Lexington Regionals . (sad face.) Arkansas' season ultimately ended in the national semifinals, and it was announced soon after that Wieber would be retiring from coaching. Her husband Chris, already on staff, takes over as the new head honcho. The Hogs will also look different athlete-wise, without the effervescent Price sisters (graduated), and Joscelyn Roberson, who transferred to Georgia in the offseason.

To end February with a bang, Mizzou will then welcome a Ryan Roberts-coached, new-look Auburn Tigers team to Columbia on Sunday, February 28 for a Week 8 matchup. Roberts was previously Georgia's co-head coach for two years, and has spent eight seasons in the SEC.

AUBURN finished last season ranked no. 25 (no. 17 in regular season) with 196.498 NQS, 196.517 average. and 197.250 high score. Their best events were vault and beam (no. 14), and weakest was bars (no. 28). The Tigers' season ended in the second round of the Baton Rouge Regional, and longtime head coach Jeff Graba departed soon after. In their last regular season meeting, Mizzou finally took a win at Neville Arena for the first time ever, earning a season-high road score of 197.325 to Auburn's 196.700. Mizzou also beat them at the SEC Championships early session.

To kick off March, the Tigers head to Iowa City to re-match Iowa for a second time this season. Per SID Ryan, the last time Missouri went to the University of Iowa was March of 2006.

To close out the regular season, the Tigers head to Baton Rouge to face the LSU Tigers on Friday, March 12.

LSU finished last season ranked no. 2 in the final polls (no. 2 in the regular season) with a 197.920 NQS and 197.865 average. Their high score was a 198.325. The Bayou Bengals finished their season with a runner up finish in the national championships, and had all events ranked in the top 3. Vault was second thanks to Kailin Chio (and others). Floor was tops nationwide, and both bars and beam were no. 3. The dueling striped cats faced each other in Columbia last year where Mizzou was woefully underscored , and the wrong Tigers narrowly won the meet, 197.675 – 197.500.

The SEC Championships will take place on March 20 and feature all nine SEC teams, with five teams in one session and four in the other. While two years ago, the Tigers made it into the night session (with higher scoring potential), they were part of the early session in 2026, finishing just behind Georgia (recap linked above).

The meet will be held in Tampa at the Benchmark International Arena, which I'm super excited about since my fam lives there! And, I should note, the Sunshine State is the home state of several Tigers, including recently retired Rayna Light (Brandon), as well as freshmen Imani White (Orlando) and Kendall Morgan (West Palm Beach).

Regionals will be held during the week of March 31 – April 4, with possible site locations in Fayetteville, Denver, Athens and Raleigh. The National Championships will be held April 15 (Semis) & 17 (Final) at Dickies Arena in Fort Worth.

Can't wait for the season to start! Bring on some intrasquads… PLEASE!

articles.title: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma Injury Report: CJ Baxter questionable; Eddy Pierre-Louis unlikely to play
articles.summary: Baxter remains questionable to play Saturday, while the Sooners get some bad news with the offensive line.
articles.body:
The Kentucky Wildcats and Oklahoma Sooners have released their second injury report ahead of Saturday's clash in Norman.

For Kentucky, Thursday's report was mostly the same as Wednesday. The big one to watch is still running back CJ Baxter, who popped up on Wednesday's report as questionable after briefly leaving last week's win over LSU with an injury. Baxter is still questionable to play.

If Baxter misses this game, Jovantae Barnes could start Saturday in what would be his return to Oklahoma for the first time since leaving the Sooners after four seasons in Norman. Jason Patterson would also be in line to see significant playing time.

Backup defensive end Tyler Thomas has now been ruled out, which is the only change for Kentucky from Wednesday's report.

For Oklahoma, the big one to watch is standout left tackle Michael Fasusi, who has been out since Week 1 but is very close to returning, which would be a massive boost against a strong Kentucky frontline. Fasusi is still listed as questionable.

The Sooners did get some bad news, as starting guard Eddy Pierre-Louis, who was listed as questionable on Wednesday, is now doubtful to play.

Wide receiver Parker Livingstone has also been downgraded from questionable to doubtful.

Add us to your "Preferred Sources" on Google to get all the latest Kentucky Wildcats news and views! And Go CATS!!

articles.body:
Florida State will try to take down the No. 3 Miami Hurricanes on Saturday, and they'll have to do so on the road where they've lost 11 straight. An updated injury report has been released, and there's one change for FSU.

Running back Sam Singleton Jr., wide receiver Devin Carter, defensive backs Karson Hobbs, Jamari Howard, and Jordan Crutchfield, plus linebackers Blake Nichelson, Izayia Williams, and Daylen Green will miss this game. Also, linebacker Noah LaVallee is out after being listed as questionable.

articles.title: No. 24 FSU soccer stuns No. 4 Wake Forest on the road
articles.summary: Ashlyn Henderson and Wrianna Hudson got on the scoresheet as No. 24 Florida State soccer beat No. 4 Wake Forest 2-0.
articles.body:
Ashlyn Henderson and Wrianna Hudson got on the scoresheet as Florida State soccer beat Wake Forest 2-0 on Thursday, Oct. 15, at Spry Stadium in Winston-Salem, North Carolina.

The No. 24 Seminoles (6-1-3) outshot the Demon Deacons 15-12 and opened the scoring in the final moment of the first half.

Henderson found herself open on a corner kick, and she steered her header into the top corner with two seconds left in the first half. It gave FSU a vital lead heading into the break, and a well-earned one, having outshot the Demon Deacons 9-6.

The Seminoles allowed Wake Forest to maintain much of the possession, but limited the scoring chances. FSU found success on the counterattack and by pressing the Demon Deacons high up the pitch, which directly led to the second goal.

Hudson picked off an errant pass from a Wake Forest defender and drove goalwards. After taking on a pair of defenders, she uncorked a left-footed strike that nestled into the top left corner to settle the outcome for the Seminoles.

What's next for FSU soccer? A road trip to Pitt

Where: Ambrose Urbanic Field / Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania

articles.title: Rams-Cardinals injury report: Kam Curl added, Jeremiyah Love still DNP
articles.summary: The Rams added Kam Curl to Thursday's injury report because of an ankle issue, while Jeremiyah Love remains out for Arizona.
articles.body:
After electing not to practice on Wednesday following Monday night's game, the Los Angeles Rams were back on the field Thursday in preparation for the Arizona Cardinals . There weren't many major changes in participation levels, but Alex Bachman was upgraded from limited to full, while Davis Allen remains sidelined by a foot injury.

The most notable change for Los Angeles was to Kam Curl. The Rams' starting safety injured his ankle in practice on Thursday and was listed as limited, an indication that he was unable to finish practice. Sean McVay will provide an update on him Friday.

Keagen Trost was also listed as a full participant in his first practice back from injured reserve.

Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love remains sidelined by an ankle injury, missing his second straight day of practice. His status for Sunday's game seems to be up in the air. Tyler Allgeier would fill in for Love at running back if he's unable to play.

There were no other changes to the Cardinals' injury report except for players who got a rest day on Wednesday and returned on Thursday.

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals' offense has been feast or (mostly) famine
articles.summary: A look at some damning offensive numbers for the Cardinals through five games.
articles.body:
A St. Louis Rams player told me many years ago that he learned a valuable lesson during his days at Penn State playing for Joe Paterno.

Defensive lineman Tyoka Jackson said Paterno would always tell the team that it was never as good as it seemed when things were going well and not as bad as it seemed when they weren't.

Of course, the reality is that the Arizona Cardinals are now 4-18 since the start of the 2025 season and it just feels very bad, especially with a 1-13 record since the middle of last season.

That doesn't mean there aren't any good things. It's simply that the bad is magnified when a game is lost like last Sunday against the Detroit Lions or in Week 2 against the Seattle Seahawks with a combined score of 76-28. The good feels only like a tease when it's followed by a sea of three-and-outs on offense or explosive plays against the defense.

As tight end Trey McBride said Wednesday about the offense, "It just feels like when we get rolling, when we get the first, first down, it's like man, our offense is really freaking good. But it's like right now it just seems like we're either on a 15-play drive or we're three-and-out. And it's like there's no in-between and that's a problem."

Some eye-opening numbers bear that out. At the end of this story will be a breakdown of the five games this season, but for now, digest these examples of feast or famine:

The Cardinals have had 18 possessions in which 15 ended with points and except for four eight-play drives (three touchdowns/one missed field goal) and one for six plays (touchdown), the other 13 all lasted at least 10 plays including nine that were 12 plays or more

In those 18 possessions, they gained 1,082 yards (60.1 yards per drive) on 196 plays (5.5 average) with 78 first downs.

The flip side has 38 possessions that gained only 424 yards (11.2 per drive) on 138 plays (3.1 average) with 21 first downs and an astounding 21 three-and-outs, not including three kneeldowns at the end of the win over the Chargers. That is the definition of famine.

McBride said, "We got to find a way to stay on the field. We have to find a way to sustain drives and when we can get that first, first down, it's like man, it almost feels like we're going to score every time. And we have to find a way to do that not only for our team, but for our defense. We can't just keep throwing them out there. 'Hey man, you just got done with a 12-play drive. All right, we'll go three-and-out.' Well, you're back up. You haven't even caught your breath yet.

"It's like we got to be better for them. We got to be better for our team. We got to find a way to get that first down and get the ball moving and score more points and get the defense off the field."

A compromised Jeremiyah Love has affected the ground game, which looked great at the beginning of the Giants game, but has gone nowhere in the last seven quarters.

"The run game's the start of everything," McBride said. "It's like if you can run the football in this league, everything else opens up. You can pass the ball better. You can do fun stuff. Everything's better when you can run the ball. So we have to find a way to run the ball.

"We have two talented running backs. Three with Bam (Knight) as well. It's like we have too many good players on this team to not be able to run the ball and it's on us as tight ends, as offensive linemen, as coaches, whatever it is, we have to be better in the run game and get that fixed."

Head coach Mike LaFleur said, "I've liked when the ball's moving and it's moving well, and then I don't like when it's stalled. We've had opportunities, particularly on offense, where it feels like it's just boom, boom, boom. Then at other times we just stall, so how can we continue to do the good stuff and not the bad? It starts with me providing that clarity, calling the right plays at the right time, and then those guys executing."

Quarterback Jacoby Brissett also spoke about the wild swings within the offense, saying, "When we haven't gone three-and-out, we've found a way to score points. It just comes down to one play at a time, finding ways to lock in and just stay on the field."

The challenge will be doing that on the road against the Rams, who are coming off a loss to the Bills in overtime Monday night. If what happened Sunday repeats itself, the noise from the fanbase will get even louder. If that's possible.

Other six possessions: 23 plays, 86 yards (3.7 per play/14.3 per possession), five first downs, two three-and-outs not including the kneeldowns.

articles.title: Granlund's Six-Game Streak Ends As Ducks Captain Hits IR List
articles.summary: Anaheim's captain Mikael Granlund is out day-to-day with an upper-body injury, ending a historic six-game point streak just as the team faces Boston.
articles.body:
On Thursday, the Anaheim Ducks confirmed that team captain Mikael Granlund is day-to-day with an upper-body injury. Just days before, the 34-year-old forward achieved the franchise record as the first player to begin a season with a six-game point streak.

The team did not specify the exact nature of the ailment, but Granlund might miss Friday night's game against the Boston Bruins. While he looked fine during Tuesday's loss to the Calgary Flames, the absence of their on-ice leader adds pressure to a roster already dealing with significant losses.

Granlund was far from invisible in his last outing. He logged 20:52 of ice time in a 4-2 defeat to the Flames and registered an assist. That single point extended his opening run to six games, a feat no other Duck has ever managed to start a season. Through the initial six games of the 2026-27 campaign, he has accumulated eight points, comprising two goals and six assists. This output places him second on the team in scoring, making his potential absence a major blow to the offense.

The timing is particularly awkward for a team that has won four of its first six games. Losing a player who averages 19:55 of ice time per game disrupts the rhythm of the top line. Per Daily Faceoff , the team announced the injury status on Thursday, leaving fans to wonder if he will be ready for the puck drop against Boston. The mystery of when the injury occurred remains unsolved, as he showed no signs of trouble during the previous match.

Granlund's status only adds to a growing list of significant names on Anaheim's injured roster. At the season's outset, Troy Terry was assigned to long-term injured reserve, which took another key scorer out of the lineup. Following a sprained MCL in last Saturday's game against the Flames, Ryan Poehling is on injured reserve and is projected to be out for 6-8 weeks. Forward Cutter Gauthier is also considered day-to-day with an upper-body injury, meaning the Ducks could be without multiple top-six forwards in a short span.

The team has managed to stay afloat despite these setbacks, but the depth is being tested early. Having the injury bug hit this early in the season could really clip their wings as they try to build on their solid start. The loss of Granlund, who has an even plus/minus so far, removes a veteran presence that helps guide younger players through the grind of an 82-game schedule.

Before this current season, Granlund had played 966 regular-season games in the NHL. During that period, he recorded 459 assists and 200 goals, totaling 659 points. His postseason experience includes 52 points accumulated across 89 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. His ability to produce at a high level has made him a natural choice for the captaincy prior to this season.

Now, the focus shifts to how the Ducks adjust without their leader. The team will need other players to step up and fill the void on the power play and in the defensive zone. If Granlund cannot play Friday, the coaching staff must find a new combination that can maintain the pace set in the first six games. The next few days will determine if this is a minor setback or the start of a longer absence for the veteran forward.

Granlund's career history shows he has handled tough situations before, but the early season timeline is critical for playoff positioning. The Ducks have won four of their first six games, a record that could slip if the top line loses its spark. Every game counts when the season is just beginning, and the loss of a eight-point leader is a hard pill to swallow for any fan base.
